# Two-user parallel public-browser verification — 4 October 2026

**Execution and narrated video verified.** Two actual Slack members supplied different harmless MDN research requests. A temporary polling dispatcher ran those requests in two separate stock Hermes `AIAgent` processes. The latest successful rerun completed both tasks correctly, with overlapping task intervals and interleaved navigation calls. Earlier runs separately measured overlapping browser-tool calls.

[Watch the 67.67-second narrated video](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Movies/clanker-two-user-2026-10-04/final/clanker-two-user-verification-narrated.mp4). It contains original Slack request footage, UTC-aligned actual worker recordings at 1x, an evidence/scope card, and ElevenLabs Hinglish narration. Worker footage is explicitly labeled as a rerun of the same verified requests. Full video/audio decoding and visual review passed; all six method pages are visible.

This is evidence for the temporary dispatcher and separate-process test architecture. It is not acceptance evidence for the existing shared Slack gateway, an OS sandbox, or complete tenant authorization.

1. **The requests came from two real Slack identities.** Saved Slack API records bind account A (`U0C684PHZ5H`) and account B (`U0C688SF7DZ`) to distinct top-level messages in workspace `T0C6J1XCDE0`, channel `C0C6J277ZNG` (`clanker-test`). Sender IDs and exact request text match the prepared test plan. [Account A request](https://clanker-global.slack.com/archives/C0C6J277ZNG/p1791122659149849) · [Account B request](https://clanker-global.slack.com/archives/C0C6J277ZNG/p1791122659695169). This audit checked the saved API records; the video shows the original posted requests, while the API evidence establishes their senders and timestamps.

2. **Each request had a separate restricted worker.** The pinned Hermes commit was `f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f`. Each worker used a fresh Hermes home/workspace, a different process, and a different dedicated Chromium endpoint. The dedicated public-worker Chromium processes were reused across recording retries and preflights; fresh Hermes homes do not imply fresh or empty browser state on each rerun. No private Slack browser state was supplied to these workers. The exact offered tools were `browser_navigate`, `browser_snapshot`, `browser_scroll`, and `browser_back`. No session search, vault, terminal, file, delegation, or typing tools were offered. Explicit navigation was restricted to `developer.mozilla.org`; that guard is not a redirect-aware network firewall. The dispatcher polled authenticated Slack history rather than opening a competing Socket Mode connection.

3. **The browser work overlapped.** Task intervals run from `task_start` to `task_result`; tool intervals run from matched `tool_start` to `tool_complete`. Calculations use the same host's recorded monotonic clock. Preparation, model initialization, Slack waiting, cleanup, and post-result recording holds are excluded. Browser-tool overlap means that browser navigation calls were simultaneously in flight; it does not measure CPU or network utilization.

| Run | Task overlap | Browser-tool overlap | Overlapping tool intervals | Outcome |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `parallel-20261004T140346Z` | N/A — no task starts in saved logs | 0 s observed | 0 | Initial dispatcher preparation failed |
| `parallel-20261004T140540Z` | 90.225843 s | 31.595991584 s | 3 | Both workers completed; 6/6 required pages; 12/12 facts correct |
| `parallel-20261004T141401Z` | N/A — neither task started | 0 s observed | 0 | Preparation could not identify one recording target |
| `parallel-20261004T141510Z` | 41.681174084 s | 4.021236625 s | 1 | Both workers completed; 6/6 required pages; 12/12 facts correct |
| `parallel-20261004T142615Z` | N/A — neither task started | 0 s observed | 0 | Recorder gate timed out; preparation failed before task execution |
| `parallel-20261004T143238Z` | 23.281013042 s | 0 s | 0 | Concurrent tasks with interleaved navigation; 6/6 required pages; 12/12 facts correct |

The `parallel-20261004T141510Z` run deliberately replayed the **same original authenticated Slack messages**; it was not a second pair of user submissions. Its 10-second post-result recording hold for each worker is excluded. The overlapping browser calls in that run were OPTIONS and DELETE, from 19:45:47.684 to 19:45:51.705 IST.

The `parallel-20261004T142615Z` attempt prepared both real browser targets, but neither received the recorder-ready acknowledgment within 150 seconds. Both exited with `TimeoutError` at approximately 19:58:49 IST before `task_start`; no model-driven browsing or answer evaluation occurred. This is a recording/preparation failure, not a measured browser-task failure. Earlier successful execution results remain separate from this unsuccessful capture attempt.

The final `parallel-20261004T143238Z` attempt again replayed the original authenticated messages. Its task intervals overlap from 20:02:51.448 to 20:03:14.729 IST, but its six short navigation calls are interleaved: **zero simultaneous in-flight browser-tool overlap was measured in this run**. Its 23.281013042-second task overlap excludes blank-tab prewarming, recorder-gate waiting, and both 10-second post-result holds. Earlier positive tool-overlap measurements must not be substituted for this run's zero measurement.

4. **The answers matched independent page evidence.** Account A requested GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS; account B requested POST, PUT, and DELETE. Each worker successfully navigated all three required official pages. All twelve Safe/Idempotent values matched both the returned browser snapshots and a separate HTTPS fetch/table parser. The oracle was fetched during the first run and reused for the rerun. Responses used three source-linked bullets rather than the requested table.

| Method | Safe | Idempotent | Official source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | Yes | Yes | [MDN GET](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Methods/GET) |
| HEAD | Yes | Yes | [MDN HEAD](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Methods/HEAD) |
| OPTIONS | Yes | Yes | [MDN OPTIONS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Methods/OPTIONS) |
| POST | No | No | [MDN POST](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Methods/POST) |
| PUT | No | Yes | [MDN PUT](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Methods/PUT) |
| DELETE | No | Yes | [MDN DELETE](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Methods/DELETE) |

5. **The tested privacy boundary was narrow.** Before execution, distinct dummy cookie values remained in their respective fresh worker browsers. This establishes that preflight cookie separation check only; it was not repeated as a post-run attack test. Both workers still run under the same OS user. Private-data authorization, hostile cross-worker access, credential revocation, private artifact sharing, stock shared-gateway behavior, hosted deployment, restart recovery, and three-user capacity remain unverified. The earlier unrestricted `session_search` finding is not resolved by this experiment.

Reviewable local evidence:

- [Latest successful rerun report](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/runs/parallel-20261004T143238Z/verification-report.json), [first-run report](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/runs/parallel-20261004T140540Z/verification-report.json), and [earlier rerun report](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/runs/parallel-20261004T141510Z/verification-report.json), including exact intervals, checked facts, absolute artifact paths, and SHA-256 hashes.
- [Latest account A events](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/runs/parallel-20261004T143238Z/A-events.jsonl) and [account B events](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/runs/parallel-20261004T143238Z/B-events.jsonl).
- [Verified actual Slack messages](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/runs/parallel-20261004T143238Z/verified-messages.json) and [latest worker results](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/runs/parallel-20261004T143238Z/results.json).
- [Independent public-page oracle](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/independent-oracle.json) and [dummy-cookie preflight](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/browser-isolation-preflight.json).
- [Recorder-gate preparation failure audit](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/runs/parallel-20261004T142615Z/verification-report.json), recording the missing task starts, zero task-tool calls, and recorder-gate timeout.

Final artifact verification: [video/audio QA and SHA-256](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Movies/clanker-two-user-2026-10-04/final/final-verification.json), [capture continuity and six page frames](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Movies/clanker-two-user-2026-10-04/final-capture-2/capture-review.json), and [edit timing manifest](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Movies/clanker-two-user-2026-10-04/final/edit-manifest.json). The final MP4 is 1920×1080 H.264 with AAC narration, 67.666667 seconds. Original browser capture is 5 fps; delivery is 30 fps with duplicate frames, without speeding up execution. Track alignment uses recorded UTC capture clocks within the source frame resolution. All three existing browser endpoints remained reachable after recording.

Earlier recording failures remain preserved separately. The first worker capture used incorrect tabs and failed encoder shutdown; the next recorded execution had a roughly 28-second capture gap and is not used as continuous execution evidence. The successful capture uses yyoreel’s screencast path, explicit stream dimensions, a six-second warmup, and activation of the owned public tabs before capturing. Narration was generated with ElevenLabs (Tara, `eleven_multilingual_v2`); the complete 56.285-second take is retained, with a 10.856-second quiet viewing interval inserted before the results commentary. No private data authorization or stock shared-gateway acceptance is established by the video.

# gateway/ — messaging gateway, adapters, delivery

Applies on top of the root `AGENTS.md`. Long-form: `website/docs/developer-guide/gateway-internals.md`.
New platform adapter: follow `gateway/platforms/ADDING_A_PLATFORM.md` step by step.

## Shape

`gateway/run.py` is the facade; phases live in `run_*.py` (startup, adapters, inbound, turn, busy,
goals, notifications, shutdown, ...), sessions in `session*.py`, slash handlers in
`slash_commands_*.py` mixins, authorization in `authz_mixin.py`, adapters in `platforms/<name>.py`
over `platforms/base.py`. `builtin_hooks/` is the extension point for always-registered gateway
hooks (none shipped). The gateway reads user YAML **raw** (`run.py` + `config.py`), not through
`DEFAULT_CONFIG` — a key the CLI sees but the gateway doesn't means you're on the wrong loader
(`hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`). Each adapter picks a base toolset (Telegram → `"messaging"`).

Slash commands: handlers are looked up by name through `_command_handler_table`; a command is
listed in `_IDLE_COMMANDS` or `_PLAIN_COMMANDS` (works mid-run) in `run_busy.py`. No
`if canonical == ...` chains. Registry + adding a command: `hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`.

## The gateway has TWO message guards — both must bypass approval/control commands

While an agent is running, an inbound message passes two sequential guards: (1) the **base
adapter** (`platforms/base.py`) queues it in `_pending_messages` when `session_key in
self._active_sessions`; (2) the **runner** (`run.py`/`run_busy.py`) intercepts `/stop`, `/new`,
`/queue`, `/status`, `/approve`, `/deny` before they reach `running_agent.interrupt()`. Any new
command that must reach the runner while the agent is blocked (approval prompts) MUST bypass BOTH
guards and be dispatched inline — never via `_process_message_background()`, which races session
lifecycle.

## Streaming delivery contract (stream-is-the-message adapters)

Adapters with `draft_stream_is_message = True` (relay Slack native streaming) keep ONE cumulative
native stream per turn; the stream IS the final message. Four invariants, each from a live
duplicate-final incident (NS-658 canary ledger, hermes#85796 / gateway-gateway#210); violating any
re-creates a duplicate or frozen stream:

1. **Draft frames are prefix-stable.** Frame N must be a string prefix of frame N+1. Never mutate
   drafts per tick — no fence-closing (`ensure_closed_code_fences`), cursor suffix, segment-state
   resets at tool boundaries, or mrkdwn conversion. A non-prefix frame forces a whole-snapshot
   re-append ("stacked copies"). The finalize path may still transform the real final.
2. **The consumer declares the final; the adapter never guesses.** `finish(final_text)` carries the
   completed `final_response` (verifier footer, completion explainer included). New post-stream
   augmentation MUST ride this payload — mutating `final_response` after the seal re-opens the
   `delivered_final_matches` mismatch → corrective duplicate send.
3. **Interim sends carry `metadata["_interim_send"] = True`.** Any consumer-side `adapter.send()`
   that is not the turn-final (commentary, segment-tail flushes) must set it or seal-interception
   seals the live stream with interim text. Seal-interception exists at BOTH egress doors (`send()`
   and `send_for_platform()`); a new egress door needs the same two checks.
4. **Reconcile by edit, never by plain send.** A lane delivering a final beside a sealed stream
   (queued follow-ups, media-accompanied finals) first tries `edit_message` on the consumer's
   `message_id`; plain `send()` only when no editable message exists. A sealed native stream is a
   regular message — `chat.update` works (live-verified).

Contract tests: `tests/gateway/test_stream_final_contract.py` (mutation-checked). Slack ground
truth: `chat.*Stream` speaks STANDARD markdown, not mrkdwn; `stopStream.markdown_text` APPENDS;
`startStream`/`stopStream` are Tier 2 (~20/min). Check `draft_stream_is_message is True` —
MagicMock adapters in older tests auto-create truthy attributes.

## Background process notifications

`terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)` starts a gateway watcher that detects
completion and triggers a new agent turn. Verbosity: `display.background_process_notifications`
(or `HERMES_BACKGROUND_NOTIFICATIONS`): `concise` (default; one line, failures append an output
tail), `all` (running updates + final raw output), `result` (final raw output only), `error`
(final raw output only on non-zero exit), `off`.

The watcher is armed on the gateway loop at registration time (`terminal_tool_background.py::
_register_completion_watcher` → `run_notifications.py::arm_process_watcher`); `pending_watchers`
is only the fallback for processes registered before the gateway serves (checkpoint recovery) or
while it stops, drained at startup and post-turn. Agent-notify watchers send no user-facing
receipt (the agent's next turn is the report) unless the launching turn is still running at exit
— then the injection only queues a follow-up, so the concise receipt goes out immediately.

The idle completion watcher also drains `watch_match` / `watch_disabled`; no user follow-up is
required. Notify-off drains these without waking. Transport failures are retried; unavailable
durable completion owners/transports do not spend delivery attempts. Profile-namespaced process
events keep their owning adapter, including raw progress/final notices. Adapter acceptance is
at-least-once admission, not proof that a model turn or final outbound reply completed. API-server
async completions remain durable delivery rows, never autonomous new model turns. Require the
`admit_internal_event` receipt for completion/watch injection: a handler returning None is not
acceptance. Refused admission refunds every claimed batch sibling without spending an attempt;
actual delivery errors keep their bounded retry policy. Recognized raw API routes resolve after
persisted messaging origins and defer quietly when unavailable; malformed routes still warn.

Cron execution has its own session. Eligible continuable deliveries may mirror or seed the
reply-facing conversation: origin, origin-less home fallback, user-written bare-platform home,
or opted-in explicit targets. `all` expansions do not gain home mirror eligibility. Mirrored
briefs are labelled user turns appended at a turn boundary, preserving role alternation
(`cron/AGENTS.md`).

## `/login` (off-turn, paired DM only)

`/login` is registered in `hermes_cli/commands.py` with `busy_policy="dispatch"` and
`desktop="settings"`, listed in `run_busy.py::_PLAIN_COMMANDS`, and handled by
`GatewayLoginCommandsMixin` (`gateway/slash_commands_login.py`). It refuses outside a paired DM:
`chat_type in {"dm","private"}`, a truthy `chat_id`, and a platform whose `"dm"` really is a paired
conversation — ntfy, raft and a2a all report `chat_type="dm"` for a broadcast topic, a channel and
an agent peer, so posting a consent link there would publish it.

**It binds the whole install.** The sign-in writes the singleton `providers.nous`, so whoever
approves the code owns this gateway's inference and connectors for every chat it serves. Slash
gating is opt-in (`gateway/slash_access.py`): with no `allow_admin_from` set, every user allowed to
DM the bot can run it. Operators of shared gateways must set it.

The handler returns its ack at once and drains `anon_auth.run_sign_in` on a **private single-worker
executor** (`_login_executor`), never the shared 10-thread gateway pool — a promotion wait can last
the code's full expiry, and a live worker in the shared pool makes shutdown skip the SessionDB
close/checkpoint. One attempt per process, stamped with the identity that started it: the same
identity's second `/login` supersedes (the loser ends with the superseded copy pushed into its own
chat); a different identity is refused. `task.cancel()` cannot interrupt a blocking poll inside a
worker thread, so shutdown and supersede both work through `attempt.cancelled`, which
`wait_for_promotion` now polls on a ≤1 s tick. A shutdown-cancelled attempt pushes nothing — the
task is dying and its adapters may already be gone — but if the server had already completed the
transfer it still persists, because that transfer is irreversible.

On completion the handler **evicts** every cached agent still on `nous/welcome` and clears any
session model override pinned to it. It does not switch agents in place and does not write a model
override: `settle_after_upgrade` already moved `model.default`/`model.base_url` in the config, every
turn re-resolves the config and the credentials, and `_agent_config_signature` already forces a
rebuild when the route changes — so an in-place swap buys no cache warmth and an override would pin
an expiring access token that nothing refreshes.

## Gateway lifecycle vs. the Desktop app

`hermes serve` (control plane, desktop-spawned child) dies with the app — by design. The messaging
gateway (`gateway run`) SURVIVES the app: the serve backend's `/api/gateway/*` endpoints spawn it
detached (`_spawn_hermes_action` — `start_new_session` / `DETACHED_PROCESS`), so `before-quit`'s
SIGTERM never reaches it and bots keep running. The known breach is the Windows shim-unlock
teardown (`taskkill /T /F` on venv-shim holders, #85265), which exists to let updates proceed and is
replaced by #92091's `pause-for-update`. Do NOT "fix" gateway-dies-with-app by re-parenting the
gateway under the backend, and do NOT "fix" update locks by widening the tree-kill. Gateways stamp
`code_sha`/`code_version` into `gateway_state.json` (`status.py`) so the updater can verify a fleet.

## Profile scope (adapters, turns, and everything between turns)

- **One identity per inbound event, canonicalized FIRST.** `gateway/session_identity.py::resolve_identity`
  answers "which bot received it / who may admit it / where does it run" ONCE per event and pins a
  frozen `RoutingIdentity` on the source (wire-invisible, like `_transport_adapter_ref`). Every

# gateway/ — messaging gateway, adapters, delivery

Applies on top of the root `AGENTS.md`. Long-form: `website/docs/developer-guide/gateway-internals.md`.
New platform adapter: follow `gateway/platforms/ADDING_A_PLATFORM.md` step by step.

## Shape

`gateway/run.py` is the facade; phases live in `run_*.py` (startup, adapters, inbound, turn, busy,
goals, notifications, shutdown, ...), sessions in `session*.py`, slash handlers in
`slash_commands_*.py` mixins, authorization in `authz_mixin.py`, adapters in `platforms/<name>.py`
over `platforms/base.py`. `builtin_hooks/` is the extension point for always-registered gateway
hooks (none shipped). The gateway reads user YAML **raw** (`run.py` + `config.py`), not through
`DEFAULT_CONFIG` — a key the CLI sees but the gateway doesn't means you're on the wrong loader
(`hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`). Each adapter picks a base toolset (Telegram → `"messaging"`).

Slash commands: handlers are looked up by name through `_command_handler_table`; a command is
listed in `_IDLE_COMMANDS` or `_PLAIN_COMMANDS` (works mid-run) in `run_busy.py`. No
`if canonical == ...` chains. Registry + adding a command: `hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`.

## The gateway has TWO message guards — both must bypass approval/control commands

While an agent is running, an inbound message passes two sequential guards: (1) the **base
adapter** (`platforms/base.py`) queues it in `_pending_messages` when `session_key in
self._active_sessions`; (2) the **runner** (`run.py`/`run_busy.py`) intercepts `/stop`, `/new`,
`/queue`, `/status`, `/approve`, `/deny` before they reach `running_agent.interrupt()`. Any new
command that must reach the runner while the agent is blocked (approval prompts) MUST bypass BOTH
guards and be dispatched inline — never via `_process_message_background()`, which races session
lifecycle.

## Streaming delivery contract (stream-is-the-message adapters)

Adapters with `draft_stream_is_message = True` (relay Slack native streaming) keep ONE cumulative
native stream per turn; the stream IS the final message. Four invariants, each from a live
duplicate-final incident (NS-658 canary ledger, hermes#85796 / gateway-gateway#210); violating any
re-creates a duplicate or frozen stream:

1. **Draft frames are prefix-stable.** Frame N must be a string prefix of frame N+1. Never mutate
   drafts per tick — no fence-closing (`ensure_closed_code_fences`), cursor suffix, segment-state
   resets at tool boundaries, or mrkdwn conversion. A non-prefix frame forces a whole-snapshot
   re-append ("stacked copies"). The finalize path may still transform the real final.
2. **The consumer declares the final; the adapter never guesses.** `finish(final_text)` carries the
   completed `final_response` (verifier footer, completion explainer included). New post-stream
   augmentation MUST ride this payload — mutating `final_response` after the seal re-opens the
   `delivered_final_matches` mismatch → corrective duplicate send.
3. **Interim sends carry `metadata["_interim_send"] = True`.** Any consumer-side `adapter.send()`
   that is not the turn-final (commentary, segment-tail flushes) must set it or seal-interception
   seals the live stream with interim text. Seal-interception exists at BOTH egress doors (`send()`
   and `send_for_platform()`); a new egress door needs the same two checks.
4. **Reconcile by edit, never by plain send.** A lane delivering a final beside a sealed stream
   (queued follow-ups, media-accompanied finals) first tries `edit_message` on the consumer's
   `message_id`; plain `send()` only when no editable message exists. A sealed native stream is a
   regular message — `chat.update` works (live-verified).

Contract tests: `tests/gateway/test_stream_final_contract.py` (mutation-checked). Slack ground
truth: `chat.*Stream` speaks STANDARD markdown, not mrkdwn; `stopStream.markdown_text` APPENDS;
`startStream`/`stopStream` are Tier 2 (~20/min). Check `draft_stream_is_message is True` —
MagicMock adapters in older tests auto-create truthy attributes.

## Background process notifications

`terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)` starts a gateway watcher that detects
completion and triggers a new agent turn. Verbosity: `display.background_process_notifications`
(or `HERMES_BACKGROUND_NOTIFICATIONS`): `concise` (default; one line, failures append an output
tail), `all` (running updates + final raw output), `result` (final raw output only), `error`
(final raw output only on non-zero exit), `off`.

The watcher is armed on the gateway loop at registration time (`terminal_tool_background.py::
_register_completion_watcher` → `run_notifications.py::arm_process_watcher`); `pending_watchers`
is only the fallback for processes registered before the gateway serves (checkpoint recovery) or
while it stops, drained at startup and post-turn. Agent-notify watchers send no user-facing
receipt (the agent's next turn is the report) unless the launching turn is still running at exit
— then the injection only queues a follow-up, so the concise receipt goes out immediately.

The idle completion watcher also drains `watch_match` / `watch_disabled`; no user follow-up is
required. Notify-off drains these without waking. Transport failures are retried; unavailable
durable completion owners/transports do not spend delivery attempts. Profile-namespaced process
events keep their owning adapter, including raw progress/final notices. Adapter acceptance is
at-least-once admission, not proof that a model turn or final outbound reply completed. API-server
async completions remain durable delivery rows, never autonomous new model turns. Require the
`admit_internal_event` receipt for completion/watch injection: a handler returning None is not
acceptance. Refused admission refunds every claimed batch sibling without spending an attempt;
actual delivery errors keep their bounded retry policy. Recognized raw API routes resolve after
persisted messaging origins and defer quietly when unavailable; malformed routes still warn.

Cron execution has its own session. Eligible continuable deliveries may mirror or seed the
reply-facing conversation: origin, origin-less home fallback, user-written bare-platform home,
or opted-in explicit targets. `all` expansions do not gain home mirror eligibility. Mirrored
briefs are labelled user turns appended at a turn boundary, preserving role alternation
(`cron/AGENTS.md`).

`/login` is registered in `hermes_cli/commands.py` with `busy_policy="dispatch"` and
`desktop="settings"`, listed in `run_busy.py::_PLAIN_COMMANDS`, and handled by
`GatewayLoginCommandsMixin` (`gateway/slash_commands_login.py`). It refuses outside a paired DM:
`chat_type in {"dm","private"}`, a truthy `chat_id`, and a platform whose `"dm"` really is a paired
conversation — ntfy, raft and a2a all report `chat_type="dm"` for a broadcast topic, a channel and
an agent peer, so posting a consent link there would publish it.

**It binds the whole install.** The sign-in writes the singleton `providers.nous`, so whoever
approves the code owns this gateway's inference and connectors for every chat it serves. Slash
gating is opt-in (`gateway/slash_access.py`): with no `allow_admin_from` set, every user allowed to
DM the bot can run it. Operators of shared gateways must set it.

The handler returns its ack at once and drains `anon_auth.run_sign_in` on a **private single-worker
executor** (`_login_executor`), never the shared 10-thread gateway pool — a promotion wait can last
the code's full expiry, and a live worker in the shared pool makes shutdown skip the SessionDB

worker thread, so shutdown and supersede both work through `attempt.cancelled`, which

task is dying and its adapters may already be gone — but if the server had already completed the
transfer it still persists, because that transfer is irreversible.

session model override pinned to it. It does not switch agents in place and does not write a model

turn re-resolves the config and the credentials, and `_agent_config_signature` already forces a
rebuild when the route changes — so an in-place swap buys no cache warmth and an override would pin
an expiring access token that nothing refreshes.

# gateway/ — messaging gateway, adapters, delivery

Applies on top of the root `AGENTS.md`. Long-form: `website/docs/developer-guide/gateway-internals.md`.
New platform adapter: follow `gateway/platforms/ADDING_A_PLATFORM.md` step by step.

## Shape

`gateway/run.py` is the facade; phases live in `run_*.py` (startup, adapters, inbound, turn, busy,
goals, notifications, shutdown, ...), sessions in `session*.py`, slash handlers in
`slash_commands_*.py` mixins, authorization in `authz_mixin.py`, adapters in `platforms/<name>.py`
over `platforms/base.py`. `builtin_hooks/` is the extension point for always-registered gateway
hooks (none shipped). The gateway reads user YAML **raw** (`run.py` + `config.py`), not through
`DEFAULT_CONFIG` — a key the CLI sees but the gateway doesn't means you're on the wrong loader
(`hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`). Each adapter picks a base toolset (Telegram → `"messaging"`).

Slash commands: handlers are looked up by name through `_command_handler_table`; a command is
listed in `_IDLE_COMMANDS` or `_PLAIN_COMMANDS` (works mid-run) in `run_busy.py`. No
`if canonical == ...` chains. Registry + adding a command: `hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`.

## The gateway has TWO message guards — both must bypass approval/control commands

While an agent is running, an inbound message passes two sequential guards: (1) the **base
adapter** (`platforms/base.py`) queues it in `_pending_messages` when `session_key in
self._active_sessions`; (2) the **runner** (`run.py`/`run_busy.py`) intercepts `/stop`, `/new`,
`/queue`, `/status`, `/approve`, `/deny` before they reach `running_agent.interrupt()`. Any new
command that must reach the runner while the agent is blocked (approval prompts) MUST bypass BOTH
guards and be dispatched inline — never via `_process_message_background()`, which races session
lifecycle.

## Streaming delivery contract (stream-is-the-message adapters)

Adapters with `draft_stream_is_message = True` (relay Slack native streaming) keep ONE cumulative
native stream per turn; the stream IS the final message. Four invariants, each from a live
duplicate-final incident (NS-658 canary ledger, hermes#85796 / gateway-gateway#210); violating any
re-creates a duplicate or frozen stream:

1. **Draft frames are prefix-stable.** Frame N must be a string prefix of frame N+1. Never mutate
   drafts per tick — no fence-closing (`ensure_closed_code_fences`), cursor suffix, segment-state
   resets at tool boundaries, or mrkdwn conversion. A non-prefix frame forces a whole-snapshot
   re-append ("stacked copies"). The finalize path may still transform the real final.
2. **The consumer declares the final; the adapter never guesses.** `finish(final_text)` carries the
   completed `final_response` (verifier footer, completion explainer included). New post-stream
   augmentation MUST ride this payload — mutating `final_response` after the seal re-opens the
   `delivered_final_matches` mismatch → corrective duplicate send.
3. **Interim sends carry `metadata["_interim_send"] = True`.** Any consumer-side `adapter.send()`
   that is not the turn-final (commentary, segment-tail flushes) must set it or seal-interception
   seals the live stream with interim text. Seal-interception exists at BOTH egress doors (`send()`
   and `send_for_platform()`); a new egress door needs the same two checks.
4. **Reconcile by edit, never by plain send.** A lane delivering a final beside a sealed stream
   (queued follow-ups, media-accompanied finals) first tries `edit_message` on the consumer's
   `message_id`; plain `send()` only when no editable message exists. A sealed native stream is a
   regular message — `chat.update` works (live-verified).

Contract tests: `tests/gateway/test_stream_final_contract.py` (mutation-checked). Slack ground
truth: `chat.*Stream` speaks STANDARD markdown, not mrkdwn; `stopStream.markdown_text` APPENDS;
`startStream`/`stopStream` are Tier 2 (~20/min). Check `draft_stream_is_message is True` —
MagicMock adapters in older tests auto-create truthy attributes.

## Background process notifications

`terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)` starts a gateway watcher that detects
completion and triggers a new agent turn. Verbosity: `display.background_process_notifications`
(or `HERMES_BACKGROUND_NOTIFICATIONS`): `concise` (default; one line, failures append an output
tail), `all` (running updates + final raw output), `result` (final raw output only), `error`
(final raw output only on non-zero exit), `off`.

The watcher is armed on the gateway loop at registration time (`terminal_tool_background.py::
_register_completion_watcher` → `run_notifications.py::arm_process_watcher`); `pending_watchers`
is only the fallback for processes registered before the gateway serves (checkpoint recovery) or
while it stops, drained at startup and post-turn. Agent-notify watchers send no user-facing
receipt (the agent's next turn is the report) unless the launching turn is still running at exit
— then the injection only queues a follow-up, so the concise receipt goes out immediately.

The idle completion watcher also drains `watch_match` / `watch_disabled`; no user follow-up is
required. Notify-off drains these without waking. Transport failures are retried; unavailable
durable completion owners/transports do not spend delivery attempts. Profile-namespaced process
events keep their owning adapter, including raw progress/final notices. Adapter acceptance is
at-least-once admission, not proof that a model turn or final outbound reply completed. API-server
async completions remain durable delivery rows, never autonomous new model turns. Require the
`admit_internal_event` receipt for completion/watch injection: a handler returning None is not
acceptance. Refused admission refunds every claimed batch sibling without spending an attempt;
actual delivery errors keep their bounded retry policy. Recognized raw API routes resolve after
persisted messaging origins and defer quietly when unavailable; malformed routes still warn.

Cron execution has its own session. Eligible continuable deliveries may mirror or seed the
reply-facing conversation: origin, origin-less home fallback, user-written bare-platform home,
or opted-in explicit targets. `all` expansions do not gain home mirror eligibility. Mirrored
briefs are labelled user turns appended at a turn boundary, preserving role alternation
(`cron/AGENTS.md`).

## `/login` (off-turn, paired DM only)

`/login` is registered in `hermes_cli/commands.py` with `busy_policy="dispatch"` and
`desktop="settings"`, listed in `run_busy.py::_PLAIN_COMMANDS`, and handled by
`GatewayLoginCommandsMixin` (`gateway/slash_commands_login.py`). It refuses outside a paired DM:
`chat_type in {"dm","private"}`, a truthy `chat_id`, and a platform whose `"dm"` really is a paired
conversation — ntfy, raft and a2a all report `chat_type="dm"` for a broadcast topic, a channel and
an agent peer, so posting a consent link there would publish it.

**It binds the whole install.** The sign-in writes the singleton `providers.nous`, so whoever
approves the code owns this gateway's inference and connectors for every chat it serves. Slash
gating is opt-in (`gateway/slash_access.py`): with no `allow_admin_from` set, every user allowed to
DM the bot can run it. Operators of shared gateways must set it.

The handler returns its ack at once and drains `anon_auth.run_sign_in` on a **private single-worker
executor** (`_login_executor`), never the shared 10-thread gateway pool — a promotion wait can last
the code's full expiry, and a live worker in the shared pool makes shutdown skip the SessionDB
close/checkpoint. One attempt per process, stamped with the identity that started it: the same
identity's second `/login` supersedes (the loser ends with the superseded copy pushed into its own
chat); a different identity is refused. `task.cancel()` cannot interrupt a blocking poll inside a
worker thread, so shutdown and supersede both work through `attempt.cancelled`, which
`wait_for_promotion` now polls on a ≤1 s tick. A shutdown-cancelled attempt pushes nothing — the
task is dying and its adapters may already be gone — but if the server had already completed the
transfer it still persists, because that transfer is irreversible.

On completion the handler **evicts** every cached agent still on `nous/welcome` and clears any
session model override pinned to it. It does not switch agents in place and does not write a model
override: `settle_after_upgrade` already moved `model.default`/`model.base_url` in the config, every
turn re-resolves the config and the credentials, and `_agent_config_signature` already forces a
rebuild when the route changes — so an in-place swap buys no cache warmth and an override would pin
an expiring access token that nothing refreshes.

## Gateway lifecycle vs. the Desktop app

`hermes serve` (control plane, desktop-spawned child) dies with the app — by design. The messaging
gateway (`gateway run`) SURVIVES the app: the serve backend's `/api/gateway/*` endpoints spawn it
detached (`_spawn_hermes_action` — `start_new_session` / `DETACHED_PROCESS`), so `before-quit`'s
SIGTERM never reaches it and bots keep running. The known breach is the Windows shim-unlock
teardown (`taskkill /T /F` on venv-shim holders, #85265), which exists to let updates proceed and is
replaced by #92091's `pause-for-update`. Do NOT "fix" gateway-dies-with-app by re-parenting the
gateway under the backend, and do NOT "fix" update locks by widening the tree-kill. Gateways stamp
`code_sha`/`code_version` into `gateway_state.json` (`status.py`) so the updater can verify a fleet.

- **One identity per inbound event, canonicalized FIRST.** `gateway/session_identity.py::resolve_identity`
  answers "which bot received it / who may admit it / where does it run" ONCE per event and pins a
  frozen `RoutingIdentity` on the source (wire-invisible, like `_transport_adapter_ref`). Every
  ingress path calls the canonicalize seam before it derives a key: the adapter side
  (`platforms/base.py::_canonicalize` — `handle_message`, `_enqueue_text_event`, Telegram photo /
  album routing, `_handle_message_while_active`, every `_source_session_key`) and the runner side

## Shape

`gateway/run.py` is the facade; phases live in `run_*.py` (startup, adapters, inbound, turn, busy,
goals, notifications, shutdown, ...), sessions in `session*.py`, slash handlers in
`slash_commands_*.py` mixins, authorization in `authz_mixin.py`, adapters in `platforms/<name>.py`
over `platforms/base.py`. `builtin_hooks/` is the extension point for always-registered gateway
hooks (none shipped). The gateway reads user YAML **raw** (`run.py` + `config.py`), not through
`DEFAULT_CONFIG` — a key the CLI sees but the gateway doesn't means you're on the wrong loader
(`hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`). Each adapter picks a base toolset (Telegram → `"messaging"`).

Slash commands: handlers are looked up by name through `_command_handler_table`; a command is
listed in `_IDLE_COMMANDS` or `_PLAIN_COMMANDS` (works mid-run) in `run_busy.py`. No
`if canonical == ...` chains. Registry + adding a command: `hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`.

## The gateway has TWO message guards — both must bypass approval/control commands

While an agent is running, an inbound message passes two sequential guards: (1) the **base
adapter** (`platforms/base.py`) queues it in `_pending_messages` when `session_key in
self._active_sessions`; (2) the **runner** (`run.py`/`run_busy.py`) intercepts `/stop`, `/new`,
`/queue`, `/status`, `/approve`, `/deny` before they reach `running_agent.interrupt()`. Any new
command that must reach the runner while the agent is blocked (approval prompts) MUST bypass BOTH
guards and be dispatched inline — never via `_process_message_background()`, which races session
lifecycle.

## Streaming delivery contract (stream-is-the-message adapters)

Adapters with `draft_stream_is_message = True` (relay Slack native streaming) keep ONE cumulative
native stream per turn; the stream IS the final message. Four invariants, each from a live
duplicate-final incident (NS-658 canary ledger, hermes#85796 / gateway-gateway#210); violating any
re-creates a duplicate or frozen stream:

1. **Draft frames are prefix-stable.** Frame N must be a string prefix of frame N+1. Never mutate
   drafts per tick — no fence-closing (`ensure_closed_code_fences`), cursor suffix, segment-state
   resets at tool boundaries, or mrkdwn conversion. A non-prefix frame forces a whole-snapshot
   re-append ("stacked copies"). The finalize path may still transform the real final.
2. **The consumer declares the final; the adapter never guesses.** `finish(final_text)` carries the
   completed `final_response` (verifier footer, completion explainer included). New post-stream
   augmentation MUST ride this payload — mutating `final_response` after the seal re-opens the
   `delivered_final_matches` mismatch → corrective duplicate send.
3. **Interim sends carry `metadata["_interim_send"] = True`.** Any consumer-side `adapter.send()`
   that is not the turn-final (commentary, segment-tail flushes) must set it or seal-interception
   seals the live stream with interim text. Seal-interception exists at BOTH egress doors (`send()`
   and `send_for_platform()`); a new egress door needs the same two checks.
4. **Reconcile by edit, never by plain send.** A lane delivering a final beside a sealed stream
   (queued follow-ups, media-accompanied finals) first tries `edit_message` on the consumer's
   `message_id`; plain `send()` only when no editable message exists. A sealed native stream is a
   regular message — `chat.update` works (live-verified).

## Background process notifications

`terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)` starts a gateway watcher that detects
completion and triggers a new agent turn. Verbosity: `display.background_process_notifications`
(or `HERMES_BACKGROUND_NOTIFICATIONS`): `concise` (default; one line, failures append an output
tail), `all` (running updates + final raw output), `result` (final raw output only), `error`
(final raw output only on non-zero exit), `off`.

The watcher is armed on the gateway loop at registration time (`terminal_tool_background.py::
_register_completion_watcher` → `run_notifications.py::arm_process_watcher`); `pending_watchers`
is only the fallback for processes registered before the gateway serves (checkpoint recovery) or
while it stops, drained at startup and post-turn. Agent-notify watchers send no user-facing
receipt (the agent's next turn is the report) unless the launching turn is still running at exit
— then the injection only queues a follow-up, so the concise receipt goes out immediately.

The idle completion watcher also drains `watch_match` / `watch_disabled`; no user follow-up is
required. Notify-off drains these without waking. Transport failures are retried; unavailable
durable completion owners/transports do not spend delivery attempts. Profile-namespaced process
events keep their owning adapter, including raw progress/final notices. Adapter acceptance is
at-least-once admission, not proof that a model turn or final outbound reply completed. API-server
async completions remain durable delivery rows, never autonomous new model turns. Require the
`admit_internal_event` receipt for completion/watch injection: a handler returning None is not
acceptance. Refused admission refunds every claimed batch sibling without spending an attempt;
actual delivery errors keep their bounded retry policy. Recognized raw API routes resolve after
persisted messaging origins and defer quietly when unavailable; malformed routes still warn.

Cron execution has its own session. Eligible continuable deliveries may mirror or seed the
reply-facing conversation: origin, origin-less home fallback, user-written bare-platform home,
or opted-in explicit targets. `all` expansions do not gain home mirror eligibility. Mirrored
briefs are labelled user turns appended at a turn boundary, preserving role alternation
(`cron/AGENTS.md`).

## `/login` (off-turn, paired DM only)

`/login` is registered in `hermes_cli/commands.py` with `busy_policy="dispatch"` and
`desktop="settings"`, listed in `run_busy.py::_PLAIN_COMMANDS`, and handled by
`GatewayLoginCommandsMixin` (`gateway/slash_commands_login.py`). It refuses outside a paired DM:
`chat_type in {"dm","private"}`, a truthy `chat_id`, and a platform whose `"dm"` really is a paired
conversation — ntfy, raft and a2a all report `chat_type="dm"` for a broadcast topic, a channel and
an agent peer, so posting a consent link there would publish it.

approves the code owns this gateway's inference and connectors for every chat it serves. Slash
gating is opt-in (`gateway/slash_access.py`): with no `allow_admin_from` set, every user allowed to
DM the bot can run it. Operators of shared gateways must set it.

transfer it still persists, because that transfer is irreversible.

session model override pinned to it. It does not switch agents in place and does not write a model
override: `settle_after_upgrade` already moved `model.default`/`model.base_url` in the config, every
turn re-resolves the config and the credentials, and `_agent_config_signature` already forces a
rebuild when the route changes — so an in-place swap buys no cache warmth and an override would pin
an expiring access token that nothing refreshes.

## Gateway lifecycle vs. the Desktop app

`hermes serve` (control plane, desktop-spawned child) dies with the app — by design. The messaging
gateway (`gateway run`) SURVIVES the app: the serve backend's `/api/gateway/*` endpoints spawn it

teardown (`taskkill /T /F` on venv-shim holders, #85265), which exists to let updates proceed and is
replaced by #92091's `pause-for-update`. Do NOT "fix" gateway-dies-with-app by re-parenting the
gateway under the backend, and do NOT "fix" update locks by widening the tree-kill. Gateways stamp
`code_sha`/`code_version` into `gateway_state.json` (`status.py`) so the updater can verify a fleet.

110	def _coerce_route_id(value: Any) -> Optional[str]:
   111	    """Normalize a route discriminator to str for strict equality matching.
   112	
   113	    PyYAML loads unquoted numeric IDs as ``int`` while ``SessionSource`` fields are ``str``. Only
   114	    ``int`` (not ``bool``) is coerced; floats stringify to something (``"123.0"``) that can never
   115	    match, so they get a load-time warning instead.
   116	
   117	    ``bool`` is an ``int`` subclass but never a valid id; floats and other types stringify to something
   118	    (``"123.0"``) that can never equal an inbound id — recreating the silent no-match this exists to fix —
   119	    so they are passed through with a load-time warning instead of being silently "fixed" (#86470).
   120	    """
   121	    if value is None or isinstance(value, str):
   122	        return value
   123	    if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool):
   124	        return str(value)
   125	    logger.warning(
   126	        "Profile route discriminator %r (type %s) can never match an inbound "
   127	        "id — quote it in config.yaml (e.g. chat_id: \"%s\").",
   128	        value, type(value).__name__, value,
   129	    )
   130	    return str(value)
   131

   134	    """Parse profile_routes from config.yaml, sorted most-specific-first."""
   135	    if not raw:
   136	        return []
   137	    routes: List[ProfileRoute] = []
   138	    for entry in raw:
   139	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
   140	            continue
   141	        name = entry.get("name", "")
   142	        platform = entry.get("platform", "")
   143	        profile = entry.get("profile", "")
   144	        if not platform or not profile:
   145	            logger.warning("Skipping profile route %s: missing platform or profile", name)
   146	            continue
   147	        # Validate profile name to prevent path traversal (lazy import: cycle).
   148	        try:
   149	            from hermes_cli.profiles import normalize_profile_name, validate_profile_name
   150	
   151	            profile = normalize_profile_name(profile)
   152	            validate_profile_name(profile)
   153	        except (ValueError, ImportError):
   154	            logger.warning("Skipping profile route %s: invalid profile name %r", name, profile)
   155	            continue
   156	        has_user_id, user_id = "user_id" in entry, entry.get("user_id")
   157	        if has_user_id and (user_id is None or isinstance(user_id, str) and not user_id.strip()):
   158	            logger.warning("Skipping profile route %s: user_id cannot be null or empty", name)
   159	            continue
   160	        routes.append(ProfileRoute(
   161	            name=name, platform=platform, profile=profile,
   162	            guild_id=_coerce_route_id(entry.get("guild_id")),
   163	            chat_id=_coerce_route_id(entry.get("chat_id")),
   164	            thread_id=_coerce_route_id(entry.get("thread_id")),
   165	            user_id=_coerce_route_id(user_id),
   166	            enabled=entry.get("enabled", True),
   167	            bot_profile=_bot_profile_key(entry.get("bot_profile")),
   168	        ))
   169	    routes.sort(key=lambda r: r.specificity, reverse=True)

# Two-user parallel public-browser verification — 4 October 2026

**Execution and narrated video verified.** Two actual Slack members supplied different harmless MDN research requests. 32	def _whatsapp_user_chat_ids_match(platform: str, left: Optional[str], right: Optional[str]) -> bool:
    33	    """True when two WhatsApp *user* chat_ids refer to the same person.
    34	
    35	    Uses ``expand_whatsapp_aliases`` (same helper as session keys and adapter allowlists) so a bare
    36	    number, JID and LID collapse to one identity. Group/broadcast JIDs are chats, not senders;
    37	    non-WhatsApp platforms → False.
    38	    """
    39	    if (
    40	        (platform or "").strip().lower() not in _WHATSAPP_IDENTITY_PLATFORMS
    41	        or not left or not right
    42	        or _is_whatsapp_non_user_chat(left) or _is_whatsapp_non_user_chat(right)
    43	    ):
    44	        return False
    45	    from gateway.whatsapp_identity import expand_whatsapp_aliases
    46	
    47	    left_aliases = expand_whatsapp_aliases(str(left))
    48	    return bool(left_aliases and left_aliases & expand_whatsapp_aliases(str(right)))

    52	    """An explicit route matched a profile this gateway does not serve."""

    58	
    59	    name: str

    61	    profile: str
    62	    guild_id: Optional[str] = None
    63	    chat_id: Optional[str] = None
    64	    thread_id: Optional[str] = None
    65	    enabled: bool = True
    66	    bot_profile: Optional[str] = None  # None = the default profile's bot
    67	    user_id: Optional[str] = None
    68

    70	    def specificity(self) -> int:
    71	        """Higher value = more specific match."""
    72	        return 2 * bool(self.guild_id) + 4 * bool(self.chat_id) + 8 * bool(self.thread_id) + 16 * bool(self.user_id)

    76	        thread_id: Optional[str] = None, parent_chat_id: Optional[str] = None,

    81	        ``chat_id`` matches the channel directly or as the parent of a thread/forum post; WhatsApp
    82	        ``chat_id`` also matches across number/JID/LID after the exact check (groups/broadcasts stay exact-only).

    93	            return False
    94	        if (
    95	            self.chat_id
    96	            and self.chat_id not in (chat_id, parent_chat_id)
    97	            and not _whatsapp_user_chat_ids_match(platform, self.chat_id, chat_id)
    98	            and not _whatsapp_user_chat_ids_match(platform, self.chat_id, parent_chat_id)
    99	        ):
   100	            return False
   101	        return not (self.guild_id and self.guild_id != guild_id)

2. Under the POC's existing isolated `HERMES_HOME`, inspect `hermes profile create --help`, then create a fresh named profile using `--no-alias --no-skills`. Do not clone a personal profile, change the OS `HOME`, or set a sticky active profile. Configure the approved model and public tools in the new profile; leave Slack bot credentials on the root transport profile.

   646	        if source.platform not in _ALLOWED_USERS_ENV:
   647	            entry = _registry_entry(source.platform)

   697	    def _get_unauthorized_dm_behavior(self, platform: Optional[Platform], *, profile: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
   698	        """How unauthorized DMs are handled ("pair" / "ignore" / "decline") for a platform.
   699	
   700	        Order: explicit per-platform config; Email → "ignore" (inboxes hold arbitrary mail); explicit
   701	        non-default global; adapter dm_policy (pairing → "pair", allowlist/disabled → "ignore"); any
   702	        configured allowlist → "ignore" (spamming unknown contacts with codes is noisy and leaks); else "pair".
   703	
   704	        1. 2. Email defaults to ``"ignore"`` unless explicitly opted into pairing. 3. Explicit global
   705	        ``unauthorized_dm_behavior`` in config — wins for chat-shaped platforms when no per-platform
   706	        override is set. 4. When an adapter-level DM policy opts into pairing or silent drop, honor it. 5.
   707	        When an allowlist (``PLATFORM_ALLOWED_USERS``, ``PLATFORM_GROUP_ALLOWED_USERS`` /
   708	        ``PLATFORM_GROUP_ALLOWED_CHATS``, or ``GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS``) is configured, default to
   709	        ``"ignore"`` — the allowlist signals that the owner has deliberately restricted access; spamming
   710	        unknown contacts with pairing codes is both noisy and a potential info-leak. (#9337) 6.
   711	        """
   712	        config = getattr(self, "config", None)
   713	        if (
   714	            config and hasattr(config, "get_unauthorized_dm_behavior") and platform
   715	            and "unauthorized_dm_behavior" in self._config_extra(platform)
   716	        ):
   717	            return config.get_unauthorized_dm_behavior(platform)
   718	        if platform == Platform.EMAIL:
   719	            return "ignore"
   720	        if config and hasattr(config, "unauthorized_dm_behavior") and config.unauthorized_dm_behavior != "pair":
   721	            return config.unauthorized_dm_behavior
   722	
   723	        allowlist_keys = ["GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS"]
   724	        if platform:
   725	            dm_policy = self._adapter_policy(platform, "dm", profile)
   726	            if not dm_policy:
   727	                dm_policy = str(self._config_extra(platform).get("dm_policy") or "").strip().lower()
   728	            if dm_policy == "pairing":
   729	                return "pair"
   730	            if dm_policy in {"allowlist", "disabled"}:
   731	                return "ignore"
   732	            # Historical: Yuanbao is absent from this allowlist-aware default.
   733	            env_key = "" if platform == Platform.YUANBAO else _ALLOWED_USERS_ENV.get(platform, "")
   734	            allowlist_keys = [env_key, _GROUP_USER_ENV.get(platform), _GROUP_CHAT_ENV.get(platform), *allowlist_keys]
   735	        if any(key and _auth_env(key).strip() for key in allowlist_keys):
   736	            return "ignore"
   737	        return "pair"

.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/features/hooks.md:1642:Auxiliary LLM calls — session titling, context compression, MoA advisors and the aggregator, vision, approval classification, memory and other side tasks — run outside the main tool-calling loop and do **not** fire `pre_api_request` / `post_api_request` (those stay turn-scoped, so a trace-per-turn plugin never sees side traffic by accident). Subscribe to `pre_auxiliary_call` / `post_auxiliary_call` instead: they fire once per physical provider attempt (retries and fallbacks included) with the same payload shape plus `aux_task` (the task name, e.g. `title_generation`, `compression`, `moa_aggregator`, `vision`). `session_id` / `task_id` / `turn_id` are the parent turn's when the call runs under one, empty otherwise; `api_request_id` (`aux-…`) is shared by every attempt of one logical call and `retry_count` distinguishes them. Both are observer-only and fail-open: a raising or timed-out callback is logged and the auxiliary task proceeds. `post_auxiliary_call` carries `error` / `error_type` when the attempt raised and `streaming: True` (with `usage`/`response` `None`) when the response is handed back as a stream.

.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/developer-guide/plugins/index.md:1059:| `post_api_request` | After each raw provider API request returns | `pre_api_request` fields plus `api_duration: float, finish_reason: str, response_model: str \| None, usage: dict, response: dict, assistant_content_chars: int, assistant_tool_call_count: int` | ignored |
.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/developer-guide/plugins/index.md:1061:| `pre_auxiliary_call` | Before each provider attempt of an auxiliary LLM call (titling, compression, MoA, vision, approval, ...); not a `pre_api_request` | `aux_task: str` plus the `pre_api_request` fields (`session_id`/`task_id`/`turn_id` are the parent turn's or empty, `api_request_id: str`, `retry_count: int`, `streaming: bool`, `request: dict`) | ignored |

.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/features/memory.md:61:The whole memory system is built around the moment a session **ends**: `MEMORY.md` and `USER.md` carry the essentials into the next session, and `session_search` fills the gaps once the old context is gone. Inside a single session none of that machinery has a reason to run — everything important is still in the live context, so the agent rarely consults `session_search` and mostly compacts memory entries instead of curating them.
.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/features/memory.md:65:**Practice:** run `/new` at natural boundaries — a finished task, a change of topic, the start of a day. Each boundary is when memory pays off: the agent re-reads the updated `MEMORY.md`/`USER.md` snapshot, starts from a cheap short context, and reaches for `session_search` when it actually needs history. On the CLI this mostly takes care of itself (every invocation is a new session); on gateways the boundary is yours to create.

.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/which-file-does-what.md:34:Memory (MEMORY.md and USER.md) is injected into the system prompt as a **frozen snapshot** captured once at session start — when the agent saves something mid-session, the change is persisted to disk immediately but won't appear in the system prompt until the next session starts. .local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/which-file-does-what.md:40:`SOUL.md` and `USER.md` are separate systems that never feed each other. `SOUL.md` is a personality file **you** edit directly — it shapes tone and identity, and its content is injected verbatim as slot #1 of the prompt. `USER.md` is part of persistent memory and is written by **the agent** through the `memory` tool. .local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/features/hooks.md:1642:Auxiliary LLM calls — session titling, context compression, MoA advisors and the aggregator, vision, approval classification, memory and other side tasks — run outside the main tool-calling loop and do **not** fire `pre_api_request` / `post_api_request` (those stay turn-scoped, so a trace-per-turn plugin never sees side traffic by accident). Subscribe to `pre_auxiliary_call` / `post_auxiliary_call` instead: they fire once per physical provider attempt (retries and fallbacks included) with the same payload shape plus `aux_task` (the task name, e.g. `title_generation`, `compression`, `moa_aggregator`, `vision`). `session_id` / `task_id` / `turn_id` are the parent turn's when the call runs under one, empty otherwise; `api_request_id` (`aux-…`) is shared by every attempt of one logical call and `retry_count` distinguishes them. Both are observer-only and fail-open: a raising or timed-out callback is logged and the auxiliary task proceeds. `post_auxiliary_call` carries `error` / `error_type` when the attempt raised and `streaming: True` (with `usage`/`response` `None`) when the response is handed back as a stream.

.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/which-file-does-what.md:34:Memory (MEMORY.md and USER.md) is injected into the system prompt as a **frozen snapshot** captured once at session start — when the agent saves something mid-session, the change is persisted to disk immediately but won't appear in the system prompt until the next session starts. This is intentional: it preserves the LLM's prefix cache for performance, and tool responses always show the live state, so nothing is lost — start a new session and the updated memory is there. Full details in [How Memory Appears in the System Prompt](./features/memory.md#how-memory-appears-in-the-system-prompt).
.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/which-file-does-what.md:38:### "I put facts about myself in SOUL.md, but USER.md stayed empty"
.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/which-file-does-what.md:40:`SOUL.md` and `USER.md` are separate systems that never feed each other. `SOUL.md` is a personality file **you** edit directly — it shapes tone and identity, and its content is injected verbatim as slot #1 of the prompt. `USER.md` is part of persistent memory and is written by **the agent** through the `memory` tool. If you want facts about yourself in USER.md, tell the agent ("remember that I prefer concise answers") and it saves them — editing SOUL.md won't populate memory, and memory entries won't change the persona. Use SOUL.md for durable voice and personality guidance; leave preferences and profile facts to memory. See [What should go in SOUL.md?](./features/personality.md#what-should-go-in-soulmd) and [Two Targets Explained](./features/memory.md#two-targets-explained).

.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/features/hooks.md:1642:Auxiliary LLM calls — session titling, context compression, MoA advisors and the aggregator, vision, approval classification, memory and other side tasks — run outside the main tool-calling loop and do **not** fire `pre_api_request` / `post_api_request` (those stay turn-scoped, so a trace-per-turn plugin never sees side traffic by accident). .local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/which-file-does-what.md:34:Memory (MEMORY.md and USER.md) is injected into the system prompt as a **frozen snapshot** captured once at session start — when the agent saves something mid-session, the change is persisted to disk immediately but won't appear in the system prompt until the next session starts. This is intentional: it preserves the LLM's prefix cache for performance, and tool responses always show the live state, so nothing is lost — start a new session and the updated memory is there. Full details in [How Memory Appears in the System Prompt](./features/memory.md#how-memory-appears-in-the-system-prompt).
.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/which-file-does-what.md:38:### "I put facts about myself in SOUL.md, but USER.md stayed empty"
.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/which-file-does-what.md:40:`SOUL.md` and `USER.md` are separate systems that never feed each other. `SOUL.md` is a personality file **you** edit directly — it shapes tone and identity, and its content is injected verbatim as slot #1 of the prompt. `USER.md` is part of persistent memory and is written by **the agent** through the `memory` tool. If you want facts about yourself in USER.md, tell the agent ("remember that I prefer concise answers") and it saves them — editing SOUL.md won't populate memory, and memory entries won't change the persona. Use SOUL.md for durable voice and personality guidance; leave preferences and profile facts to memory. See [What should go in SOUL.md?](./features/personality.md#what-should-go-in-soulmd) and [Two Targets Explained](./features/memory.md#two-targets-explained).

.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/features/hooks.md:1642:Auxiliary LLM calls — session titling, context compression, MoA advisors and the aggregator, vision, approval classification, memory and other side tasks — run outside the main tool-calling loop and do **not** fire `pre_api_request` / `post_api_request` (those stay turn-scoped, so a trace-per-turn plugin never sees side traffic by accident). Subscribe to `pre_auxiliary_call` / `post_auxiliary_call` instead: they fire once per physical provider attempt (retries and fallbacks included) with the same payload shape plus `aux_task` (the task name, e.g. `title_generation`, `compression`, `moa_aggregator`, `vision`). `session_id` / `task_id` / `turn_id` are the parent turn's when the call runs under one, empty otherwise; `api_request_id` (`aux-…`) is shared by every attempt of one logical call and `retry_count` distinguishes them. Both are observer-only and fail-open: a raising or timed-out callback is logged and the auxiliary task proceeds. `post_auxiliary_call` carries `error` / `error_type` when the attempt raised and `streaming: True` (with `usage`/`response` `None`) when the response is handed back as a stream.

.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/features/memory.md:61:The whole memory system is built around the moment a session **ends**: `MEMORY.md` and `USER.md` carry the essentials into the next session, and `session_search` fills the gaps once the old context is gone. Inside a single session none of that machinery has a reason to run — everything important is still in the live context, so the agent rarely consults `session_search` and mostly compacts memory entries instead of curating them.
.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/features/memory.md:65:**Practice:** run `/new` at natural boundaries — a finished task, a change of topic, the start of a day. Each boundary is when memory pays off: the agent re-reads the updated `MEMORY.md`/`USER.md` snapshot, starts from a cheap short context, and reaches for `session_search` when it actually needs history. On the CLI this mostly takes care of itself (every invocation is a new session); on gateways the boundary is yours to create.

.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/which-file-does-what.md:16:| **USER.md** | User profile — your name, role, preferences, communication style, expectations | The agent, via the `memory` tool (you can gate saves with `write_approval`, or edit entries via `hermes journey edit`) | Injected into the system prompt as a frozen snapshot at session start | `~/.hermes/memories/` |

.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/which-file-does-what.md:34:Memory (MEMORY.md and USER.md) is injected into the system prompt as a **frozen snapshot** captured once at session start — when the agent saves something mid-session, the change is persisted to disk immediately but won't appear in the system prompt until the next session starts. This is intentional: it preserves the LLM's prefix cache for performance, and tool responses always show the live state, so nothing is lost — start a new session and the updated memory is there. Full details in [How Memory Appears in the System Prompt](./features/memory.md#how-memory-appears-in-the-system-prompt).
.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/which-file-does-what.md:38:### "I put facts about myself in SOUL.md, but USER.md stayed empty"
.local/hermes-lab/upstream/website/docs/user-guide/which-file-does-what.md:40:`SOUL.md` and `USER.md` are separate systems that never feed each other. `SOUL.md` is a personality file **you** edit directly — it shapes tone and identity, and its content is injected verbatim as slot #1 of the prompt. `USER.md` is part of persistent memory and is written by **the agent** through the `memory` tool. If you want facts about yourself in USER.md, tell the agent ("remember that I prefer concise answers") and it saves them — editing SOUL.md won't populate memory, and memory entries won't change the persona. Use SOUL.md for durable voice and personality guidance; leave preferences and profile facts to memory. See [What should go in SOUL.md?](./features/personality.md#what-should-go-in-soulmd) and [Two Targets Explained](./features/memory.md#two-targets-explained).

   138	        _set_extra_header(api_kwargs, "x-initiator", "user")
   139	        agent._is_user_initiated_turn = False
   140	    try:
   141	        from hermes_cli.middleware import apply_llm_request_middleware
   142	
   143	        _llm_request_mw = apply_llm_request_middleware(
   144	            api_kwargs, task_id=effective_task_id, turn_id=turn_id, api_request_id=api_request_id,
   145	            session_id=agent.session_id or "", platform=agent.platform or "", model=agent.model,
   146	            provider=agent.provider, base_url=agent.base_url, api_mode=agent.api_mode,
   147	            api_call_count=api_call_count,
   148	        )
   149	        api_kwargs = _llm_request_mw.payload
   150	        _original_api_kwargs = _llm_request_mw.original_payload
   151	        _llm_middleware_trace = _llm_request_mw.trace
   152	    except Exception:
   153	        _original_api_kwargs = dict(api_kwargs)
   154	        _llm_middleware_trace = []
   155	
   156	    _fire_pre_api_request_hook(
   157	        agent, api_kwargs, api_messages, _llm_middleware_trace, messages=messages,
   158	        original_user_message=original_user_message, approx_tokens=approx_tokens,
   159	        total_chars=total_chars, retry_count=retry_count, api_call_count=api_call_count,
   160	        api_request_id=api_request_id, api_start_time=api_start_time,
   161	        effective_task_id=effective_task_id, turn_id=turn_id,
   162	    )
   163	
   164	    if env_var_enabled("HERMES_DUMP_REQUESTS"):

   168	    # none serializes it into the provider payload. Re-read the live client:
   169	    # rotation/fallback/cleanup rebuild agent.client between attempts; a native OpenAI
   170	    # client rejects this key (TypeError).

   264	The same `list` / `delete <id>` / `edit <id>` subcommands work from the in-chat `/journey` command on the CLI, and the desktop panel offers edit/delete on nodes directly.
   265	
   266	## Configuration
   267	
   268	```yaml
   269	# In ~/.hermes/config.yaml
   270	memory:
   271	  memory_enabled: true
   272	  user_profile_enabled: true
   273	  memory_char_limit: 2200   # ~800 tokens
   274	  user_char_limit: 1375     # ~500 tokens
   275	  write_approval: false     # false = write freely (default) | true = require approval
   276	```
   277	
   278	Setting **both** `memory_enabled` and `user_profile_enabled` to `false` turns the
   279	built-in stores off completely: the `memory` tool is dropped from the schema and
   280	its guidance block is dropped from the system prompt, so the model is never told
   281	about a tool it cannot use. An external provider set via `memory.provider`
   282	(Hindsight, Mem0, Honcho, …) is unaffected and keeps its own tools — use this
   283	when you want a third-party memory backend *instead of* the built-in files.
   284	Listing `memory` under `agent.disabled_toolsets` is the heavier switch: it hides
   285	external provider tools too.
   286	
   287	With only `memory_enabled: false` (user profile still on), the tool stays —
   288	it backs the profile store — but the system prompt swaps the full memory
   289	guidance for a narrower profile-only block. The tool schema advertises only the
   290	`user` target, and direct or staged writes to disabled `MEMORY.md` are rejected.
   291	The inverse configuration advertises only `memory` and rejects `USER.md` writes.
   292	
   293	## Controlling memory writes (`write_approval`)
   294	
   295	By default the agent saves memory freely — including from the background
   296	self-improvement review that runs after a turn. If you'd rather approve saves
   297	first, set `memory.write_approval: true`. It's a simple on/off gate applied to
   298	**both** foreground turns and the background review:

   300	| `write_approval` | Behaviour |

"""Abstract base class for pluggable memory providers.

Plugins ship in ``plugins/memory/<name>/``, activated via ``memory.provider`` (ONE external
provider at a time). Lifecycle, driven by MemoryManager: initialize -> system_prompt_block /
prefetch / sync_turn per turn -> tool dispatch -> shutdown, plus optional ``on_*`` hooks.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextvars
import logging
import re
import threading
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def ctx_bound(fn: Callable[..., Any]) -> Callable[..., Any]:
    """Bind ``fn`` to the CALLER's contextvars for another thread/executor. Profile isolation
    is a ContextVar-scoped HERMES_HOME override plus the per-turn secret scope; a worker started
    with an empty context silently lands on the default profile (or fails closed on secrets)."""
    ctx = contextvars.copy_context()
    return lambda *args, **kwargs: ctx.run(fn, *args, **kwargs)


def spawn_context_thread(target: Callable[..., Any], *, name: str, daemon: bool = True,
                         args: tuple = (), kwargs: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> threading.Thread:
    """Unstarted thread running *target* under the spawner's contextvars (see :func:`ctx_bound`).
    Every memory-provider background job (prefetch, sync, writer loops) must go through this."""
    return threading.Thread(target=ctx_bound(target), args=args, kwargs=kwargs, name=name, daemon=daemon)

# v1 = best-effort on_pre_compress() with the raw message list; v2 = opt-in fail-closed
# checkpoint (normalized evidence handoff + strict-mode failure propagation).
PRE_COMPRESS_CHECKPOINT_API_VERSION = 2

# Default glyph for recall indicators; providers may use their own brand mark.
INDICATOR_GLYPH = "🧠"

# ``memory.provider`` values that mean "the built-in store, no external plugin". The built-in
# store is core: doctor, migration and dependency refresh must never look these up as plugins.
CORE_MEMORY_PROVIDER_SENTINELS = frozenset({"", "default", "builtin", "built-in", "none"})


def is_core_memory_provider(name: Optional[str]) -> bool:
    """True when ``memory.provider`` selects the built-in store rather than an external plugin."""
    return str(name or "").strip().lower() in CORE_MEMORY_PROVIDER_SENTINELS


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RecallStatus:
    """What the last prefetch injected, for the deterministic recall indicator
    (``MemoryManager.describe_recall``). ``count == 0`` means content without a
    discrete count (e.g. a synthesized reflect answer) and renders generically."""

    provider_label: str
    count: int
    glyph: str = INDICATOR_GLYPH


# Prompts with no semantic signal; single source of truth for the core prefetch gate and
# provider-side classifiers. Anchored and followed only by whitespace/punctuation, so
# "k8s"/"yolo"/"note" do NOT match while "hi!"/"thanks :)"/"done???" do.
TRIVIAL_PROMPT_RE = re.compile(
    r'^(yes|no|ok|okay|sure|thanks|thank you|y|n|yep|nope|yeah|nah|'
    r'hi|hey|hello|yo|sup|'
    r'continue|go ahead|do it|proceed|got it|cool|nice|great|done|next|lgtm|k)'
    r'[\s!?.:;,"' + "'" + r'~\u2018\u2019\u201c\u201d\u2014\u2013\u2026()\[\]{}<>*&^%$#@!+=`\u00a0]*$',
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def is_trivial_prompt(text: Optional[str]) -> bool:
    """True for empty input, slash commands and bare greetings/acknowledgements (skipping
    recall saves a round-trip and keeps stale context from derailing one-word replies)."""
    stripped = (text or "").strip()
    if not stripped or stripped.startswith("/"):
        return True
    return bool(TRIVIAL_PROMPT_RE.match(stripped))

    def handle_tool_call(self, tool_name: str, args: Dict[str, Any], **kwargs) -> str:
        """Handle one of this provider's tools; must return a JSON string."""
        raise NotImplementedError(f"Provider {self.name} does not handle tool {tool_name}")

    def on_turn_start(self, turn_number: int, message: str, **kwargs) -> None:
        """Per-turn tick. kwargs may include remaining_tokens, model, platform, tool_count, author_id, author_name,

    def get_config_schema(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:

        optional ``secret`` (goes to .env), ``required``, ``default``, ``choices``, ``type``

import re

def ctx_bound(fn: Callable[..., Any]) -> Callable[..., Any]:
    """Bind ``fn`` to the CALLER's contextvars for another thread/executor. Profile isolation
    is a ContextVar-scoped HERMES_HOME override plus the per-turn secret scope; a worker started
    with an empty context silently lands on the default profile (or fails closed on secrets)."""
    ctx = contextvars.copy_context()
    return lambda *args, **kwargs: ctx.run(fn, *args, **kwargs)
